primary_statutes: Assembly Bill 1482 (AB 1482) — Tenant Protection Act of 2019
_metadata.statutory_retrieval_note: CCP §1161 and Civil Code §1946.2 verified via Legal Data Hunter live retrieval on 2026-05-30. Source: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov. CCP §1161 operative Feb 1, 2025 (amended by SB 611, Stats. 2024). AB 1482 (Civil Code §1946.2) amended by AB 1529 (Stats. 2025) — IMPORTANT: repealed as of January 1, 2030 unless extended.
_metadata.ab1482_sunset_warning: Civil Code §1946.2 (AB 1482) is repealed as of January 1, 2030 per its own provisions. Monitor for legislative extension.
_metadata.portability_note: This file is the CA-specific rules layer. The reasoning engine is jurisdiction-agnostic. Swap this file for tx_eviction_rules.json or ny_eviction_rules.json to apply the same logic to Texas or New York.

nonpayment_of_rent.notice_type: 3-Day Notice to Pay Rent or Quit
nonpayment_of_rent.notes: Days do not count Saturdays, Sundays, or judicial holidays per CCP §12a. AB 2347 (eff. Jan 1, 2025) extended tenant response time from 5 to 10 business days to respond to an unlawful detainer summons after service — this is the court response window, not the notice period itself.

defect_triggers.description: Notice includes late fees, utilities, or any charge other than unpaid rent
defect_triggers.rule: The notice amount must reflect ONLY unpaid rent. Including late fees, utility charges, or any other amount in the demanded sum renders the notice void.

defect_triggers.description: Notice served before rent is legally delinquent (within grace period)
defect_triggers.rule: If the lease provides a grace period before rent is considered delinquent, the notice cannot be served until that period has expired.

defect_triggers.description: Notice charges tenant a fee for serving, posting, or delivering the notice
defect_triggers.rule: CCP §1161(6) explicitly prohibits a landlord or its agent from charging the tenant any fee for serving, posting, or delivering any eviction notice. Such a charge renders the notice defective.

defect_triggers.description: Incorrect rent amount stated — overstates or understates actual unpaid rent
defect_triggers.rule: The notice must state the exact amount of rent owed. Any material error in the amount can void the notice.

curable_lease_violation.notice_type: 3-Day Notice to Perform Covenant or Quit
curable_lease_violation.notes: Must cite the specific lease clause violated. If tenant does not cure, landlord must serve a SECOND separate 3-Day Notice to Quit (unconditional) before filing unlawful detainer.

defect_triggers.description: Notice does not cite the specific lease clause allegedly violated
defect_triggers.rule: The notice must identify the specific covenant or condition of the lease that was breached.

defect_triggers.description: Landlord filed UD without serving a second unconditional 3-Day Notice to Quit after cure period expired
defect_triggers.rule: After a 3-Day Notice to Perform or Quit, if the tenant does not cure, landlord must serve a separate 3-Day Notice to Quit before filing. Filing after only the first notice is premature.

unconditional_quit.notes: For incurable violations — criminal activity, nuisance, waste, subletting without permission. No cure opportunity is provided.

defect_triggers.description: Unconditional notice used for a curable violation
defect_triggers.rule: Unconditional 3-Day Notices are only valid for incurable violations. Using one for a curable lease violation (e.g., unauthorized pet) may be defective.

no_fault_short_tenancy.applies_when: Month-to-month tenancy of less than 1 year
no_fault_short_tenancy.notes: Under AB 1482, if the unit is covered and tenant has lived there 12+ months, this notice is insufficient — landlord must use 60-day notice with just cause. See ab1482 section below.

defect_triggers.description: 30-day notice served on tenant who has lived in unit 1 year or more
defect_triggers.rule: Tenants who have continuously resided in a unit for 1 year or more are entitled to 60-day notice. A 30-day notice to such a tenant is defective.

no_fault_long_tenancy.notes: Under AB 1482, covered units with no-fault terminations also require: (1) a stated just cause reason, and (2) relocation assistance equal to 1 month's rent.

defect_triggers.description: AB 1482 covered unit: no-fault notice does not state just cause reason
defect_triggers.rule: For units covered under AB 1482 where tenant has 12+ months, no-fault notices must state a qualifying just cause reason. Missing this makes the notice defective.

defect_triggers.description: AB 1482 covered unit: no-fault notice does not include relocation assistance statement
defect_triggers.rule: No-fault terminations in AB 1482-covered units require relocation assistance equal to 1 month's rent. Failure to provide or offer this can be a defense.

subsidized_housing.notes: Federal overlay applies. Section 8 and HUD tenants have additional federal protections beyond state law.

defect_triggers.description: Subsidized housing tenant given less than 90-day notice
defect_triggers.rule: Tenants in government-subsidized housing (Section 8, HUD) are entitled to a minimum 90-day notice regardless of state notice minimums.

ellis_act_withdrawal.applies_when: Landlord withdrawing entire property from rental market
ellis_act_withdrawal.notes: Ellis Act withdrawals require 120-day notice (1 year for seniors and disabled tenants). Strict procedural requirements — landlord must file with local rent board.

defect_triggers.description: Ellis Act notice given to senior (62+) or disabled tenant without extended 1-year notice period
defect_triggers.rule: Tenants who are 62 or older or who are disabled are entitled to a 1-year notice period under the Ellis Act.

alternative_methods.description: If tenant not home, leave with person of suitable age AND mail a copy. Both steps required.
alternative_methods.condition: Only if personal service not possible after reasonable attempt

alternative_methods.description: If neither tenant nor suitable person found, post on main entrance AND mail a copy.
alternative_methods.condition: Only if substituted service not possible

defect_triggers.description: Improper service method — wrong method used or required steps not followed
defect_triggers.rule: Personal delivery is required first. Substituted service requires BOTH leaving with a person AND mailing. Post-and-mail requires BOTH posting AND mailing. Using a lesser method without exhausting required alternatives renders the notice period invalid — the clock does not start running.

defect_triggers.description: Notice period counted from wrong date (e.g., from mailing date rather than posting/delivery date)
defect_triggers.rule: For post-and-mail service, the notice period begins running from the date of posting, not mailing. Error in calculating the start date can make the filing premature.

ab1482_just_cause.statute: Civil Code §1946.2 (AB 1482 — Tenant Protection Act of 2019)
ab1482_just_cause.coverage_note: AB 1482 applies to most residential rental units in California where the tenant has lived for 12 or more months. Significant exemptions exist.
exemptions: Single-family homes where owner provides required written exemption notice
Condominiums sold separately from other units where owner provides required written exemption notice
Units built within the last 15 years (rolling exemption)
Owner-occupied buildings with 2 or fewer units (duplex where owner lives on site)
Units subject to local rent control ordinance that provides equivalent or greater just cause protections
at_fault_just_cause_reasons: Breach of material lease term after notice to cure
Assigning or subletting contrary to lease
Refusal to execute written extension on similar terms
Refusal of lawful entry after proper notice
no_fault_just_cause_reasons: Owner or owner's spouse/parent/child/grandparent moving in (owner move-in — OMI)
Substantial remodel (requires permits; cannot be pretextual)

no_fault_relocation_requirement.timing: Must be paid at or before the time of service of the termination notice, or landlord waives right to terminate
no_fault_relocation_requirement.alternative: Landlord may waive final month's rent in lieu of relocation payment

defect_triggers.description: AB 1482 covered unit: notice does not state a qualifying just cause reason
defect_triggers.rule: For tenants covered under AB 1482 (12+ months, non-exempt unit), any termination notice must state a qualifying at-fault or no-fault just cause reason. A notice without just cause is void.

defect_triggers.description: No-fault just cause termination without relocation assistance
defect_triggers.rule: No-fault terminations in AB 1482-covered units require 1 month's relocation assistance. Failure to pay at or before service of notice is a defense.

defect_triggers.description: Landlord claims AB 1482 exemption but did not provide required written exemption notice to tenant
defect_triggers.rule: For SFH and condo exemptions, landlord must have provided a written notice of exemption to the tenant at or before the inception of the tenancy or when the exemption first became applicable. Failure to give required notice may mean exemption does not apply.

coverage_determination_questions: How many months has the tenant continuously resided in the unit?
Is the unit a single-family home or condo? If so, did the landlord provide a written exemption notice?
When was the unit built? (If within 15 years, may be exempt)
Does the owner live in the same building in a 2-unit building?
Is the unit subject to local rent control with equivalent protections?

affirmative_defenses.name: Warranty of Habitability
affirmative_defenses.description: Landlord failed to maintain the unit in habitable condition. Tenant may withhold rent proportionally for breach of implied warranty of habitability.
examples: No working windows or exterior doors
documentation_needed: Written repair requests to landlord (texts, emails, letters)
Code enforcement complaints or inspection reports
affirmative_defenses.interaction_with_rent_nonpayment: If landlord failed to maintain habitable conditions, tenant's obligation to pay full rent may be reduced or eliminated proportionally. This is a complete or partial defense to a nonpayment eviction.

affirmative_defenses.name: Retaliation
affirmative_defenses.description: Landlord is evicting because tenant exercised a legal right: complained to code enforcement, reported habitability issues to landlord in writing, organized with other tenants, or requested repairs.
affirmative_defenses.presumption: If eviction occurs within 180 days of tenant exercising a protected right, retaliation is PRESUMED. Burden shifts to landlord to prove a non-retaliatory reason.
protected_tenant_activities: Complaining to code enforcement or housing authority
Exercising rights under lease or law
Organizing or participating in tenant association
Testifying before government body about housing

affirmative_defenses.name: Discrimination
affirmative_defenses.description: Eviction is motivated by tenant's protected characteristic.
statutes: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
protected_classes_ca: Sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression
Source of income (including Section 8 vouchers — CA state law)

affirmative_defenses.name: Rent Accepted After Notice (Waiver)
affirmative_defenses.description: Landlord accepted rent payment AFTER serving the eviction notice. This may waive the notice and require landlord to start over.
affirmative_defenses.strength: MODERATE — depends on facts and lease terms
affirmative_defenses.notes: Even partial rent acceptance can waive a nonpayment notice. Some leases include anti-waiver clauses — their enforceability varies.

affirmative_defenses.name: Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA) Application Pending
affirmative_defenses.description: Tenant applied for Emergency Rental Assistance; local rules may require landlord to apply for ERA and wait for determination before evicting.
affirmative_defenses.notes: ERA protections vary significantly by city and county. Check whether local moratorium or ERA participation requirement applies.

affirmative_defenses.name: Domestic Violence / Protected Status
affirmative_defenses.description: Tenant is a survivor of domestic violence and the acts underlying the eviction are related to abuse.
affirmative_defenses.notes: Tenant may terminate a lease early or assert this as a defense to eviction without penalty. Documentation (police report, protective order, declaration) typically required.

affirmative_defenses.name: Local Rent Control / Just Cause Ordinance
affirmative_defenses.description: City or county ordinance provides additional protections beyond AB 1482 — e.g., Los Angeles RSO, San Francisco Rent Ordinance, Oakland Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance.
affirmative_defenses.strength: STRONG where applicable — may be stronger than state law
major_local_ordinances: Los Angeles: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) — applies to most pre-1978 multi-unit buildings
San Francisco: Rent Ordinance — strong just cause requirements, additional protected categories
Oakland: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance
Santa Monica: Rent Control Charter Amendment
Berkeley: Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance
affirmative_defenses.notes: CRITICAL: Always check local ordinance in addition to state law. Many CA cities have protections that significantly exceed AB 1482.

notice_analysis: What type of notice was served? (3-day pay or quit / 3-day to perform or quit / 30-day / 60-day / other)
What is the exact dollar amount stated in the notice?
Does the notice include any amounts other than unpaid rent? (late fees, utilities, other charges)
What city and county is the rental unit in?
How long has the tenant continuously lived in the unit? (months/years)
Is the unit a single-family home or condo?
How was the notice served? (handed directly / left with someone / posted on door / mailed)
What date was the notice served?
Has the landlord accepted any rent payment since serving the notice?
Has the tenant made any written complaints about repairs or habitability in the past 6 months?
Has the tenant contacted code enforcement or any government agency about the unit in the past year?
Are there any known habitability issues with the unit? (mold, pests, heat, plumbing)

local_overlays_flag.instruction: If the unit is in one of these cities, flag that additional local ordinance research is required before providing a final analysis.
